clue.text: Chivalrous group ranked by their results?

definitions.meaning: an honour conferred by the monarch, membership of a select order limited to a few dozen distinguished people
a list placing candidates by how well they performed, best first

explanation.surface: A band of knights seems to be lined up according to their scores.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is both a British royal honour, a select order, and a ranking that places people by performance.

clue.text: Vehicle serving a number of purposes

definitions.meaning: an old name for a bus carrying many passengers
as an adjective, covering or including many different things at once

explanation.surface: A versatile vehicle that can be used for several jobs.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names an old-fashioned bus and, as an adjective, describes something that includes many items.

clue.text: Mates in game, superficially bouncy

definitions.meaning: male and female waterfowl, pairs of birds that mate together
the pastime of skimming flat stones so they bounce along the surface of water

explanation.surface: Partners in a sport that skips lightly along.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Superficially' is meant literally: the stones bounce on the water's surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Female and male birds of the duck family are partners, and the phrase also names the stone-skimming pastime.

clue.text: Country artist appearing in convention briefly

indicators.note: the artist is seen inside the shortened convention, so these words place one piece within another
cut short, so the last letter of the synonym for convention is dropped

parts.note: a convention is a rule or custom
RA stands for Royal Academician, an artist

explanation.surface: A painter turns up, for a short while, at a gathering out of town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Country' looks like a nation, but here it is the adjective meaning of the countryside.
explanation.definitionFit: Used adjectivally, country describes things belonging to the countryside, rather than to the town.

clue.text: Waved proudly and ran to embrace relative

indicators.note: to hug, so one word wraps around the other piece here

parts.note: ran away means fled
an aunt is a relative

explanation.surface: Someone showed off by rushing to hug a family member.
explanation.definitionFit: To show something off ostentatiously, such as a banner, is to display it proudly.

clue.text: Account book with no margins? Just one

indicators.note: lacking its borders, so the first and last letters of the synonym are dropped

parts.note: a ledger is a book of accounts

explanation.surface: A bookkeeper's volume printed without any margins, apart from one.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition plays on 'margins': a single border or rim is just one margin.
explanation.definitionFit: A margin is a border or rim, so a single border is just one of them.

clue.text: In compost, mushrooms raised for one to check

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: lifted up, which in a down clue reads the two pieces from bottom to top

parts.note: rot is decaying matter such as compost
ceps are a kind of edible mushroom

explanation.surface: Fungi are grown in a compost heap for someone to examine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raised' turns ROT + CEPS backwards as a whole run, giving SPECTOR.
explanation.definitionFit: An inspector is an official whose job is to examine and verify things.

clue.text: To lap, wave needs means to detach from current

parts.note: a circuit is one lap around a track
a breaker is a wave that crashes on the shore

explanation.surface: A swimmer completing a lap must cope with a breaking wave dragging them out on the current.
explanation.walkthrough: 'current' looks like a sea current but is electric current.
explanation.definitionFit: This safety device automatically disconnects an electrical supply, cutting a circuit off from its current.

clue.text: Man rowing on holiday throws wife finally into ravine

indicators.note: pitches something in, together with into placing one piece inside another
the letter goes inside the ravine word, placing one piece within another

parts.note: a gorge is a deep ravine

indicators.note: the last letter of the word wife is taken

explanation.surface: A holidaymaker in a boat pitches his spouse into a canyon.
explanation.walkthrough: This man is one of Jerome K Jerome's Three Men in a Boat, a comic novel about a boating holiday on the Thames.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Victorian comic novel, one of the three friends rowing up the Thames bears this name.

clue.text: New freezer is better

parts.note: an icer is something that freezes or ices

explanation.surface: A newly bought freezer is an improvement.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words are comparatives meaning more pleasant or superior.

clue.text: Missionary imposing fine for beheading

parts.note: august means grand, impressive or imposing

indicators.note: losing its head, so the word fine drops its first letter

explanation.surface: A missionary demands a penalty for an execution.
explanation.walkthrough: 'imposing' looks like a verb with 'fine' as object, but it is an adjective meaning grand.
explanation.definitionFit: Saint Augustine of Canterbury was the monk sent by the Pope to convert the English in 597.

clue.text: It's smashing to keep learner busy

indicators.note: to hold, so the learner letter is held inside the other word

parts.note: busting means smashing or breaking
L is for learner, as on a learner driver's L-plate

explanation.surface: A remark that it is great fun to keep a trainee occupied.
explanation.definitionFit: A scene full of energetic activity is busy, crowded with movement.

clue.text: One with flashing blade that secures a boundary

definitions.meaning: a swordsman in the sport of foil, epee or sabre
someone who puts up enclosures round land

explanation.surface: A swordsman who also guards a frontier.
explanation.definitionFit: A fencer both fights with a sword in sport and, literally, builds fences enclosing land.

clue.text: Creepy relative held at home

indicators.note: contained, so the word for at home sits inside the relative

parts.note: a sister is a relative
in means at home

explanation.surface: A spooky family member is kept indoors.
explanation.definitionFit: Something sinister is menacing and threatening, giving an unsettling, creepy feeling.

clue.text: Resist having to leave seat closed

parts.note: to stand up is to rise and leave your seat
to, as in a door pulled to, means closed

explanation.surface: Someone stops getting up because the seat has been folded shut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to', of a door, means pushed shut.
explanation.definitionFit: To confront and refuse to give way to someone is to resist them.

clue.text: New priest's mark of rank

indicators.note: signals that the letters of priest are made new, rearranged into another word

parts.note: the 's only shows possession or stands for 'is', so it adds no letters: the word before it gives these letters as it is written

explanation.surface: A newly ordained priest's badge of seniority.
explanation.definitionFit: A stripe on a uniform sleeve is a badge showing military rank.

clue.text: Role for acolyte I further developed

indicators.note: worked into a new form, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An altar server advancing in their duties.
explanation.definitionFit: A thurifer carries the censer of incense in a church service, a task often given to an acolyte.

clue.text: Adjust descriptions of skin after abrasion

parts.note: grazed skin is red
grazed skin is raw

explanation.surface: Doctors adjusting the notes describing a graze.
explanation.definitionFit: To redraw something, such as boundaries, is to draw it again and so adjust it.

clue.text: Healthy old boy wearing reddish-brown

indicators.note: dressed in, so the old boy goes inside the colour

parts.note: rust is a reddish-brown colour
OB is short for old boy, a former pupil

explanation.surface: A fit former pupil dressed in russet.
explanation.definitionFit: Robust means strong and vigorous, in good health.

clue.text: Angelic woman's come into the equation

indicators.note: to enter, so the woman's word goes inside the equation word

parts.note: a cubic is an equation of the third degree
her is the woman's, a possessive pronoun

explanation.surface: A woman is now a factor to be considered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'come into the equation' is an idiom for becoming relevant; here it is literal.
explanation.definitionFit: Cherubic means like a cherub, a kind of angel, so innocently angelic.

clue.text: A collier heartlessly made to work, generating a bit of heat

indicators.note: set to work, so the letters are moved about into a new order
without its heart, so the middle letter of collier is removed

explanation.surface: A miner is cruelly forced to work, producing warmth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartlessly' removes the central L of COLLIER, leaving COLIER; with A that is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A calorie is a unit measuring a small quantity of heat energy.

clue.text: Alcohol makes bishop lascivious

parts.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop
randy means lustful or lascivious

explanation.surface: Drink turns a cleric lecherous.
explanation.definitionFit: Brandy is a spirit distilled from wine, an alcoholic drink.

clue.text: Protector made mark during argument in prison

indicators.note: goes inside the prison word, placing one piece within another

parts.note: a cell is a prison room

indicators.note: in the course of, so the mark sits within the argument

parts.note: a row is an argument
M is short for mark, the old German currency

explanation.surface: A man left a mark in the course of a quarrel behind bars.
explanation.walkthrough: Oliver Cromwell was Lord Protector of England in the 1650s. 'made' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Oliver Cromwell ruled England, Scotland and Ireland with the title Lord Protector.

clue.text: Correspondence game

definitions.meaning: agreement or likeness between two things

explanation.surface: A game played by post.
explanation.definitionFit: A match is both a close resemblance and a sporting contest.

clue.text: Girl-meets-officer shock

parts.note: Jo is a girl's name
LT is the abbreviation for lieutenant, an officer

explanation.surface: A girl dating an officer causes a scandal.
explanation.definitionFit: A jolt is a sudden jerk or shock.

clue.text: Gets rid of hangover, perhaps, a result of Duncan's murder?

definitions.meaning: recovers from too much drink by resting
King Duncan was killed in his sleep in Shakespeare's Macbeth, so he died while asleep

explanation.surface: A man recovers from a heavy night, linked jokingly to a famous killing in Shakespeare.
explanation.walkthrough: In Macbeth, King Duncan is murdered in bed while asleep; the phrase is read literally as dropping off for good.
explanation.definitionFit: To cure a hangover by sleeping it away is the idiom; Duncan literally slept and was gone.

clue.text: Could be a thief, one's prepared to bet

definitions.meaning: someone who accepts a wager offered

explanation.surface: A gambler who might also steal.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names one who takes, such as a thief, and one who accepts a bet.

clue.text: Novel way to get throne?

parts.note: doctoring, that is rearranging, the letters of a certain surname yields the word throne

explanation.surface: A clue asking how to seize a crown.
explanation.walkthrough: A reverse clue: an anagram signal followed by fodder makes the clue's last word. The novel is by Anthony Trollope.
explanation.definitionFit: Doctor Thorne is an 1858 novel by Anthony Trollope, one of his Barsetshire series.
